about: Every external source, data store, processing step and page of cosh, and the flows between them. Read by web/dataflow.html, scripts/dataflow.py (check, plan) and `python3 -m cosh update`. Field meanings and the flow rules: docs/data-architecture.md. Keep it current: CLAUDE.md, Conventions. Building and deploying the site (npm run build; the Pages workflow on push) is not a data step and isn't listed.

sources.name: Chromium Gerrit
sources.purpose: Code review of chromium/src: CL listings over REST, each CL's review comments and events as its NoteDb ref, and its uploaded patch sets.
sources.access: Anonymous; every request carries the contact e-mail (data/private/settings.json or COSH_CONTACT).
sources.load_rules: REST serial, at least 1 s apart; NoteDb in batches of 200 refspecs, one fetch at a time; patch sets with glob refspecs only (never ls-remote or blobs by id), up to 7 fetches at once, pausing together on a 429. Backoff on 429/5xx; one extractor at a time (data/private/extract.lock).
sources.coverage: chromium/src main (master before 2021-05): CLs closed 2017-W27 .. 2026-W44 plus an open-CL snapshot; patch sets of reviewed CLs closed 2023-W26 .. 2026-W44. The approved ranges are config/approved.json, which the fetchers enforce.
sources.notes: Three channels of one host: REST (listings, accounts), NoteDb (refs/changes/NN/N/meta) and patch-set refs (refs/changes/NN/N/<ps>).

sources.name: Chromium git
sources.purpose: Chromium's git history on main: commits, authors, files touched, footers and file contents.
sources.access: Anonymous git over HTTPS with the contact e-mail; main only, no tags.
sources.load_rules: One fetch of main at a time, under data/private/extract.lock. Other branches or repos need approval.
sources.coverage: All of main, with full blobs (approved 2026-11-06 and 2026-11-07).

sources.name: Affiliations file
sources.purpose: affiliations.json5 (dated e-mail-to-employer overrides used to attribute each person to an organisation) and org-list.txt beside it.
sources.access: Anonymous GET with the contact headers.
sources.load_rules: Two small requests per `cosh update-affiliations` run (the one step that fetches them); no approval needed.

sources.name: Claude
sources.purpose: Labels and scores text that rules can't: addressed threads, comment tone, AI-written descriptions, coaching reports.
sources.access: The user's Claude Max login; untrusted text only through cosh.sandbox.Sandbox (no tools, scrubbed env, bwrap jail).
sources.load_rules: Costs Max usage: size each run (--week, --max-threads, --dry-run) first. Not Gerrit load, so calls may run in parallel.
sources.coverage: Haiku for bulk labels; Opus for audits and coaching reports.

sources.name: Cloudflare Radar
sources.purpose: Daily share of human web requests per browser (all devices, and iOS alone) and per OS.
sources.access: API token in CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, from `source ~/.secrets/cosh/secrets.sh`; never printed or committed.
sources.load_rules: Serial, at least 1 s apart; complete quarters are never refetched. A weekly update is about 3 requests.
sources.coverage: 2023-06-26 (Radar's first data) to the day of the last run.

sources.name: Chromium issue tracker
sources.purpose: Metadata (type, priority, severity, component, status) of the bugs named in commit footers and security release notes.
sources.access: Anonymous POST to an undocumented endpoint; restricted bugs are silently left out (about 46% of asked IDs are visible).
sources.load_rules: Searches serial with no wait, 50 IDs each; backs off 5/15/30 min on 429, 5xx or network errors; stops on a captcha.
sources.coverage: 147,407 bug IDs from Bug:/Fixed: footers on main since 2023-07-01 and from Chrome Releases security fixes.

sources.name: Monorail stubs
sources.purpose: Redirect pages that map pre-2024 Monorail bug IDs to their new tracker IDs.
sources.load_rules: Up to 4 at once with no wait; any 429, 5xx or network error stops all workers and backs off.
sources.coverage: All 21,267 Monorail-era IDs wanted as of 2026-11-08.

sources.name: Chrome Releases blog
sources.purpose: Release posts listing each security fix's CVE, bug ID and severity.
sources.access: Anonymous GET; post bodies are parsed by regex only and never shown to a model.
sources.load_rules: Serial, at least 2 s apart, 150 posts per page; cached pages are not refetched without --refresh.

stores.name: gerrit.sqlite + notedb/
stores.purpose: Everything fetched from Gerrit, losslessly: gerrit.sqlite caches every REST response and which weeks are done; notedb/ holds each CL's NoteDb ref, the only copy of comment text and review events.
stores.files: gerrit.sqlite; notedb/chromium_src.git, a bare repo with a ref refs/meta/<CL> per fetched CL (about 716k).

tables.name: responses
tables.purpose: Every REST response, compressed, keyed by host, kind and key.

columns.kind: What was fetched: list_window (a CL listing), comments (one CL's review data), or account (one user).
columns.key: Identifies the request: the listing window spec, or the change or account number.
columns.fetched_at: When it was fetched, UTC time, ISO 8601.
columns.http_status: HTTP status code of the response.
columns.body_zlib: The response body, zlib-compressed, with Gerrit's XSSI prefix removed.
columns.body_sha256: SHA-256 hash of the response body, to detect changes.

tables.name: week_progress
tables.purpose: Per ISO week: when it was listed and when all its NoteDb refs were fetched.

columns.iso_week: The ISO week, e.g. 2026-W44, whose closed CLs were listed.
columns.listed_at: When the week's CL listing finished, UTC time, ISO 8601; empty until listed.
columns.cl_count: Number of CLs listed for the week.
columns.fetched_at: When all of the week's review data finished downloading, UTC time, ISO 8601; empty if not done.
columns.last_run_id: The extract_runs.run_id of the latest run that worked on this week.

tables.name: week_changes
tables.purpose: Which listing response holds each CL of each week.

columns.iso_week: The ISO week the CL closed in.
columns.window_key: Key of the responses row (kind list_window) whose JSON holds this CL.

tables.name: open_listings
tables.purpose: Open-CL snapshots and their progress.

columns.listed_at: When this snapshot of open CLs started, UTC time, ISO 8601; identifies the snapshot.
columns.since: The snapshot includes open CLs updated at or after this time, UTC, ISO 8601.
columns.closed_since: The snapshot also includes CLs closed at or after this time, UTC, ISO 8601.
columns.cl_count: Number of CLs in the snapshot.
columns.fetched_at: When all of the snapshot's review data finished downloading, UTC time, ISO 8601; empty if not done.
columns.last_run_id: The extract_runs.run_id of the latest run that worked on this snapshot.

tables.name: open_changes
tables.purpose: Which listing response holds each CL of an open snapshot.

columns.listed_at: The open_listings.listed_at snapshot this CL belongs to.
columns.window_key: Key of the responses row (kind list_window) whose JSON holds this CL.

tables.name: extract_runs
tables.purpose: One row per extractor run: arguments, times, request count.

columns.run_id: Sequential number of the extraction run.
columns.started_at: When the run started, UTC time, ISO 8601.
columns.finished_at: When the run ended, UTC time, ISO 8601; empty while running.
columns.command: The command line that was run.
columns.requests: Number of requests the run sent to Gerrit.
columns.status: Outcome: running, ok, partial, failed or interrupted.

stores.notes: Never delete either, never prune or gc notedb/. Lossless repacks only (cosh notedb-maintain, scripts/notedb_chunked_repack.sh). Comment text is untrusted.

stores.purpose: Per-CL, per-comment and per-thread facts without comment text; the input to nearly every analysis.

tables.name: changes
tables.purpose: One row per CL: branch, owner, status, times, close week, size, bot flag.

columns.change_id: Gerrit Change-Id, the I-prefixed hash from the commit message footer.
columns.owner_account: Account number of the CL's author; joins accounts.account_id.
columns.created_at: When the CL was created, UTC, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.
columns.updated_at: When the CL last changed, UTC, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.
columns.submitted_at: When the CL merged, UTC, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS; empty unless merged.
columns.closed_at: Merge time, or last update time if abandoned, UTC; empty if open.
columns.close_week: ISO week of closed_at, e.g. 2026-W44; empty if open.
columns.patchsets: Number of patch sets (uploaded revisions) of the CL.
columns.total_comment_count: Total inline comments on the CL, as Gerrit reports it.
columns.is_bot_owned: 1 if a bot account owns the CL, else 0.
columns.subject: First line of the CL description.
columns.anchor_path: File with the most inline comments on the CL; empty if none.

tables.name: comments
tables.purpose: One row per published comment by someone other than the owner on a human-owned CL: week, path, length, AI flag.

columns.change_number: Gerrit CL the comment is on.
columns.comment_id: Gerrit's unique id (UUID) of the comment.
columns.account_id: Account number of the commenter; joins accounts.account_id.
columns.written_at: When the comment was written, UTC, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.
columns.path: File the comment is on, or /PATCHSET_LEVEL or /COMMIT_MSG for general comments.
columns.chars: Comment length in characters, not counting quoted lines.
columns.is_ai: 1 if written by an AI reviewer (AI flag or autogenerated tag), else 0.
columns.after_close: 1 if written after the CL merged or was abandoned, else 0.
columns.root_uuid: Id of the first comment in this comment's thread.

tables.name: threads
tables.purpose: Reviewer-started threads: size, owner's last reply, the regex verdict and the hash that keys labels.

columns.change_number: Gerrit CL the thread is on.
columns.root_uuid: Id of the thread's first comment.
columns.root_account: Account number of the reviewer who started the thread.
columns.n_comments: Number of comments in the thread, including the author's replies.
columns.last_owner_reply_at: When the CL author last replied in the thread, UTC; empty if never.
columns.input_hash: Hash of the thread text a model would see; matches labels.input_hash.
columns.regex_addressed: 1 if the author's first reply is a 'Done'-style answer, else 0.

tables.name: accounts
tables.purpose: Gerrit accounts: e-mail, name, bot flag.

columns.name: The account's display name.
columns.is_bot: 1 if the account is a bot, else 0.

tables.name: committers
tables.purpose: Which accounts may vote Code-Review, as of the newest listing.

columns.is_committer: 1 if the account may vote Code-Review in chromium/src, else 0.
columns.seen_at: When Gerrit reported this status, UTC time, ISO 8601.

tables.name: meta
tables.purpose: Metric version, fetched weeks, when it was derived.

columns.k: Name of the setting, e.g. metric_version, derived_at, fetched_weeks.

stores.notes: Rebuild: rm it, then `python3 -m cosh derive` (about 9 min).

stores.purpose: Haiku's addressed / not-addressed label for each review thread the regex doesn't settle.

tables.name: labels
tables.purpose: Addressed 0/1 per thread, classifier and input hash.

columns.change_number: Gerrit CL the thread is on.
columns.root_uuid: Id of the thread's first comment.
columns.classifier_id: Which classifier made the label; joins classifiers.classifier_id.
columns.input_hash: Hash of the thread text that was classified; matches threads.input_hash.
columns.addressed: 1 if the thread's comment was addressed by the author, else 0.
columns.run_id: The runs.run_id of the run that produced this label.

tables.name: classifiers
tables.purpose: Model, definition version and prompt hash; the newest matching the code is active.

columns.classifier_id: Sequential id of this classifier setup.
columns.model: Claude model that classifies, e.g. claude-haiku-5-5.
columns.definition_version: Version number of the 'addressed' definition and prompt.
columns.prompt_sha256: SHA-256 hash of the prompt text.
columns.created_at: When the classifier was first used, UTC time, ISO 8601.

tables.name: runs
tables.purpose: Each classify run's weeks, threads, calls, tokens and cost.

columns.run_id: Sequential number of the classification run.
columns.started_at: When the run started, UTC time, ISO 8601.
columns.finished_at: When the run ended, UTC time, ISO 8601; empty if unfinished.
columns.weeks: JSON list of the ISO weeks the run covered.
columns.threads: Number of threads labelled in the run.
columns.tokens: Total tokens used by the model calls.
columns.usd_equiv: Equivalent cost in US dollars at API prices; actual use is on a subscription.
columns.seconds: Total time spent in model calls, in seconds.

stores.purpose: The fetch ranges the user has approved; extract, backfill, patchsets and cosh.bugs refuse anything outside them.
stores.notes: Widen a range only after the user approves, with a docs/plan.md decision in the same commit.

stores.purpose: Verbatim copies of Chromium's affiliations.json5 and org-list.txt, with a note of where and when they were fetched.
stores.notes: Written only by the affiliations step; OrgResolver() reads the local copy and never fetches. Commit them with the outputs when they change.

stores.purpose: Hand-kept e-mail patterns that mark bot accounts and bot commit authors.
Hand-kept directory rules: which paths the contribution metrics count, and the directory tree's roots.

stores.name: Value Exchange data
stores.purpose: Weekly contribution by organisation, person and directory for all 487 fetched weeks: everything Value Exchange shows except usage.

tables.name: org_weekly.json
tables.purpose: Per week and org: reviewers, CLs, comments, addressed comments, commits; plus the meta block. 3.4 MB.

tables.name: weekly_totals.csv
tables.purpose: Per week: CLs merged, abandoned, by humans and bots.

columns.iso_week: Week the CLs closed, ISO week label like 2025-W45 (Monday to Sunday)
columns.main_cls: CLs on branch main that closed (merged or abandoned) that week
columns.merged_cls: Of those, number that were merged
columns.abandoned_cls: Of those, number that were abandoned
columns.human_cls: Of those, number owned by a person rather than a bot
columns.bot_cls: Of those, number owned by a bot account
columns.human_cls_with_comments: Human-owned CLs that got at least one review comment from a non-bot

tables.name: reviewer_weekly.json
tables.purpose: Every reviewer's weekly counts, for the leaderboard. 4.8 MB.

tables.name: author_weekly.json
tables.purpose: Every commit author's weekly commits. 5.0 MB.

tables.name: area_weekly.json
tables.purpose: Comments per week, directory and org. 12 MB.

tables.name: area_reviewers.json
tables.purpose: Who wrote each directory's comments. 16 MB.

tables.name: area_commits.json
tables.purpose: Commits per week, directory and org. 14 MB.

tables.name: area_authors.json
tables.purpose: Who made each directory's commits. 32 MB.

tables.name: thread_examples.json
tables.purpose: Example threads per outcome, with comment text (untrusted). 0.4 MB.

tables.name: classifier_prompt.json
tables.purpose: The addressed-classifier prompt, shown on the page.

stores.purpose: The 800-thread audit of the addressed classifier: the threads and Opus's labels, so it can be rerun.

stores.name: Patch-set commits
stores.files: Bare repo with refs/patchsets/<CL>/<ps>; main's objects come from the shared clone through git alternates.
stores.purpose: Every patch-set commit of reviewed CLs with its blobs, for diffing one patch set against the next.
stores.notes: Never prune. A whole-repo repack runs out of memory: repack in groups (scripts/patchsets_chunked_repack.sh). The W44 pilot repo (chromium-src.git) was retired on 2026-11-13: all its objects are here; its ref names are kept in data/private/git/chromium-src-pilot-refs.txt.

stores.files: <series>_all_1d_<start>_<end>.json, one per calendar quarter, for series browser, browser_ios and os.
stores.purpose: Verbatim cache of every Radar response, committed so the share CSV can be rebuilt offline.
stores.notes: A refresh rewrites the three files of the current quarter.

stores.purpose: A one-off probe of a jump in Radar's ChromeDerivative share, behind docs/radar-research.md.
stores.notes: Written by the two scripts inside it. Nothing reads it.

stores.name: Browser shares
stores.purpose: Each browser's weekly and monthly share of requests, with iOS removed and renormalised among Chromium browsers.

columns.period: Week (like 2025-W45) or month (like 2025-11) the share covers
columns.period_start: First day of the period, UTC, YYYY-MM-DD
columns.period_end: Last day of the period, UTC, YYYY-MM-DD
columns.device: Device class the share covers; currently all (non-iOS devices combined)
columns.browser: Browser name as Cloudflare Radar reports it
columns.is_chromium: 1 if the browser is Chromium-based, 0 if not; empty if unclassified
columns.kind: Client type: browser, webview, in_app, tv, bot or other; empty if unclassified
columns.days: Number of daily data points in the period (fewer than a full week or month at the edges)
columns.raw_share: Share of human, non-iOS requests from this browser, mean of daily shares, 0-1
columns.chromium_share: Browser's share among counted Chromium browsers only, 0-1; empty if not counted

stores.purpose: Hand-kept list of Radar's browser names: which are Chromium-based and which count in the usage denominator.

columns.browser: Browser name as Cloudflare Radar reports it
columns.is_chromium: 1 if the browser is built on Chromium, else 0
columns.kind: Client type: browser, webview, in_app, tv, bot or other
columns.notes: Short explanation of how the browser is classified

stores.purpose: Hand-kept map from each organisation to the browsers credited to it; the page joins usage to orgs with it.

columns.org_domain: Organization's domain, as used in affiliations
columns.browser: Radar browser name that the organization ships
columns.notes: Short explanation of why this browser is attributed to the organization

stores.files: comments-<week>.jsonl (52 weeks) and comments-sample-5pct.jsonl, with identities.
stores.purpose: Review comments rendered with their thread context and who wrote them: the input to scoring, praise and the Feedback Index's excerpts.
stores.notes: Holds untrusted comment text. One writer (comments-collect).
stores.name: Rendered comments
stores.withheld: Review comments with who wrote them, the input to tone scoring; tone stays unpublished per person (ground rule 5).

stores.purpose: Haiku's tone score (-1 .. +1) and AI-friction flag for each scored comment, and the cached identifying-detail screening verdicts.

tables.name: scores
tables.purpose: Score, AI flag and the model's reason per comment, prompt and input hash.

columns.id: Comment id: Gerrit CL number, a slash, then the comment UUID.
columns.prompt_id: Which prompt scored it; joins prompts.prompt_id. 0 means a bare acknowledgement scored without a model.
columns.input_hash: Hash of the text the model saw.
columns.score: Tone of the comment from -1 (hostile) through 0 (neutral) to +1 (strong gratitude).
columns.ai: 1 if the comment expresses negative feeling about AI in code review, else 0.
columns.why: The model's short reason for the score.

tables.withheld: Tone scores and the model's reasons per comment; only praise and anonymous samples are published (ground rule 5).

tables.name: prompts
tables.purpose: The prompt version, hash and model the scores were made with.

columns.prompt_id: Sequential id of the scoring prompt.
columns.sha256: SHA-256 hash of the prompt text.
columns.model: Model that scores with this prompt, e.g. haiku.
columns.created_at: When the prompt was first used, UTC time, ISO 8601.

tables.name: screens
tables.purpose: Screening verdicts (does a comment identify someone), keyed by comment and screen prompt; written by tone-publish as a cache.

columns.id: Comment id: Gerrit CL number, a slash, then the comment UUID.
columns.screen_sha: SHA-256 hash of the screening prompt used.
columns.flagged: 1 if the screen found identifying details in the comment, else 0.

tables.withheld: Screening verdicts on negative comments (ground rule 5).

stores.notes: Per-comment reasons stay private.

stores.name: Prompt-tuning results
stores.purpose: The 261 hand-labelled gold comments (ids and scores, no text) and each prompt version's scores against them.
stores.notes: gold.jsonl is hand-made and not rebuildable; it stays private (docs/sentiment.md).
stores.withheld: The hand-labelled gold sets stay private.

stores.name: Scoring prompts
stores.purpose: The tone-scoring prompts; the page shows v3.
stores.notes: Editing the current prompt changes its hash, so every comment would need rescoring.

stores.name: Review Tone data
stores.purpose: Everything Review Tone shows: the monthly trend, praise boards, sample comments, per-period detail and the person-search list. Negative comments only anonymously.

tables.name: sentiment_monthly*.json
tables.purpose: Monthly tone trend: mean score and shares of glowing, grumpy and AI-friction comments.

tables.name: sentiment_praise*.json
tables.purpose: Praise leaderboards and who-praises-whom counts, by person; positive totals only.

tables.name: sentiment_samples*.json
tables.purpose: Sample comments per tone band: praise with links, negative ones anonymous after screening.

tables.name: sentiment_{recent,comments}*.json
tables.purpose: The score distribution per period, the anonymous AI-friction comments, and each person's praise comments for the name popups.

tables.name: sentiment_people.json
tables.purpose: Names and e-mails of the people on the praise boards, for the page's person search.

stores.notes: Each family but sentiment_people has three files: committers (no suffix), .everyone and .noncommitters.

stores.name: Chromium git clone
stores.purpose: Bare mirror of chromium/src main with full blobs, shared across argus's projects; cosh only reads it and fetches main into it.
stores.notes: Outside cosh (~/projects/shared/README.md): keep it a clean mirror, no cosh refs or local edits, never prune or gc. cosh's patch-set repo borrows its objects through git alternates. Read it with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1.

stores.purpose: Every first-parent commit of main since 2008 with its files and line counts, LSC tags, OWNERS additions and repetition ratios: the one store of git history that every step reads.

tables.name: commits
tables.purpose: Commits: author, times, CL, Reviewed-by, reverts, relands, Bot-Commit, AI-marker and LSC (large-scale change) flags, files and lines. commit_id counts up from 1 at 2017-01-01 and down from -1 before.

columns.commit_id: Landing order on main, from 1 (first commit since 2017-01-01).
columns.authored_at: When the commit was authored, Unix seconds.
columns.landed_at: When the commit landed (committer date), Unix seconds.
columns.change_number: Gerrit CL number from the Reviewed-on footer; empty if none.
columns.is_bot: 1 if the commit has a Bot-Commit footer, else 0.
columns.reviewed_by: JSON list of lowercased emails from Reviewed-by footers; empty if none.
columns.reverts_sha: Hash of the commit this one reverts, from its This reverts commit line.
columns.is_reland: 1 if the subject starts with Reland, else 0.
columns.files: Number of files changed in the commit's first-parent diff.
columns.is_revert: 1 if a message line starts This reverts commit, else 0.
columns.ai_marker: 1 if the commit message carries an AI-assistance marker, else 0.
columns.is_lsc: 1 if the commit is part of a large-scale change, found by its message, else 0.

tables.name: commit_files
tables.purpose: Files per commit with line counts.

columns.ins: Lines added in this file; -1 for a binary file.

tables.name: paths
tables.purpose: Path dictionary for commit_files.

columns.path_id: Integer id of a file path, used by commit_files.
columns.path: File path within the Chromium repository, relative to its root.

tables.name: owners_added
tables.purpose: Each address on a line added to an OWNERS file.

columns.commit_id: Foreign key to commits.commit_id (the commit that added the owner).
columns.seq: Order of the addition within the commit's diff.
columns.email: Email added to an OWNERS file, lowercased.
columns.path: The OWNERS file the address was added to.

tables.name: repetition
tables.purpose: Repetition ratio of each commit with a CL and 10 or more files (mechanical CLs).

columns.ratio: 1 minus distinct changed lines over changed lines; near 1 means the same edit repeated. Empty if too large.

tables.name: gcommits
tables.purpose: View: the commits since 2017-01-01 (commit_id > 0), the per-CL window.

columns.commit_id: Landing order of the commit on main (1 = first commit since 2017-01-01).
columns.authored_at: When the commit was authored, Unix seconds.
columns.landed_at: When the commit landed (committer date), Unix seconds.
columns.change_number: Gerrit CL number from the Reviewed-on footer; empty if none.
columns.is_bot: 1 if the commit has a Bot-Commit footer, else 0.
columns.reviewed_by: JSON list of lowercased emails from Reviewed-by footers; empty if none.
columns.reverts_sha: Hash of the commit this one reverts, from its This reverts commit line.
columns.is_reland: 1 if the subject starts with Reland, else 0.
columns.files: Number of files changed in the commit's first-parent diff.

tables.name: gfiles
tables.purpose: View: their files.

columns.path_id: Foreign key to paths.path_id (the changed file).
columns.ins: Lines added in this file; -1 for a binary file.

stores.notes: Rebuildable: delete it and rerun (about 1 h 50 min). $COSH_COMMITS_DB overrides the path (docs/commits.md).

stores.purpose: Each CL's patch-set uploads, attention-set changes and Code-Review votes, read from its NoteDb event log in one walk.

tables.name: uploads
tables.purpose: One row per uploaded patch set: who and when.

columns.ps: Patch set number within the CL.
columns.at: When the patch set was uploaded, Unix seconds.
columns.uploader: Gerrit account id of the uploader.
columns.kind: Upload type: initial, rework, rebase, message_only or no_change.
columns.sha: Git commit hash of the patch set.

tables.name: attention
tables.purpose: Attention-set changes: whose turn it was and when.

columns.account_id: Gerrit account id of the person in the attention set.
columns.start_at: When the account entered the attention set, Unix seconds.
columns.end_at: When it left, or the CL closed or was last updated, Unix seconds.

tables.name: votes
tables.purpose: Code-Review vote events: who, when, value, patch set.

columns.voter: Gerrit account id of the voter.
columns.value: Code-Review vote from -2 to +2; 0 means the vote was removed.
columns.at: When the vote was cast, Unix seconds.
columns.ps: Patch set the vote applied to.

tables.name: timeline_done
tables.purpose: CLs read, with their meta ref's tip then; a CL whose tip moved is read again.

columns.tip: Hash of the CL's NoteDb meta ref when read; CL is reread if it changes.

stores.purpose: Lines changed between consecutive patch sets: how much each CL was reworked during review.

tables.name: interdiff
tables.purpose: Per CL and patch-set pair: lines added and deleted, files.

columns.seen_ps: Patch set the reviewer first saw (the one reviewed).
columns.final_ps: Last patch set of the CL.
columns.lines_seen: Changed lines in the reviewed patch set's diff.
columns.lines_final: Changed lines in the final patch set's diff.
columns.lines_changed: Changed lines present in one diff but not the other; rebases count 0.
columns.files_changed: Number of files whose diff differs between the two patch sets.
columns.files_added: Files in the final diff but not the reviewed one.
columns.files_dropped: Files in the reviewed diff but not the final one.
columns.status: ok, missing (patch sets not stored locally) or too_big (diff too large to compare).

stores.purpose: One wide row per CL joining the stages: author and reviewer effort, latency, rework, comments, addressed labels.

tables.name: cl
tables.purpose: Per CL: 36 columns of size, timing, review and outcome facts.

columns.owner: Gerrit account id of the CL owner.
columns.status: CL state: MERGED, ABANDONED or NEW.
columns.created_at: When the CL was created, Unix seconds.
columns.closed_at: When the CL was merged or abandoned, Unix seconds; empty while open.
columns.close_week: Week in which the CL closed, as an ISO week label such as 2021-W14.
columns.ins: Lines added in the final patch set, per Gerrit (renames detected).
columns.dels: Lines deleted in the final patch set, per Gerrit.
columns.sha: Hash of the commit that landed on main; empty if not landed.
columns.files: Number of files in the landed commit.
columns.git_lines: Lines added plus deleted in the landed commit (no rename detection).
columns.is_revert: 1 if the landed commit is a revert, else 0.
columns.is_reland: 1 if the landed commit is a Reland, else 0.
columns.reverted_at: When the first commit reverting the landed commit landed, Unix seconds.
columns.comments: Number of review comments by non-bot accounts before close.
columns.reviewers: Number of distinct accounts that commented.
columns.threads: Number of comment threads started by non-bot accounts.
columns.addressed: Threads whose comment the owner addressed, per the regex and Claude classifier.
columns.pending: Threads not yet classified as addressed or not.
columns.first_review_at: First substantive review (inline comment or answered reviewer thread), Unix seconds.
columns.sent_at: First time a non-owner entered the attention set, Unix seconds.
columns.rework_after: Rework uploads after the first review.
columns.rounds: Owner rework uploads after sending that follow a new reviewer-started thread.
columns.reviewer_wait_h: Hours some non-owner human was in the attention set.
columns.reviewer_wait_wd_h: Same as reviewer_wait_h, leaving out Saturdays and Sundays (UTC).
columns.owner_wait_h: Hours the owner was in the attention set.
columns.seen_ps: Patch set the reviewer first saw, as in the interdiff table.
columns.lines_seen: Changed lines in the reviewed patch set's diff.
columns.lines_final: Changed lines in the final patch set's diff.
columns.lines_changed: Changed lines present in one diff but not the other.
columns.files_changed: Files whose diff differs between reviewed and final patch sets.
columns.files_added: Files in the final diff but not the reviewed one.
columns.interdiff_status: Interdiff result: ok, missing or too_big.

tables.name: cl_attention
tables.purpose: Per CL and person: time in the attention set.

columns.account_id: Gerrit account id of a non-owner human.
columns.hours: Hours that account was in the CL's attention set.
columns.weekday_hours: The same hours with Saturdays and Sundays (UTC) left out.

tables.name: cl_dirs
tables.purpose: Directories each CL touches.

columns.dir: Directory of the landed commit, cut to three levels, with trailing slash.
columns.files: Files of the landed commit in that directory.
columns.lines: Lines changed by the landed commit in that directory.

stores.purpose: Commits on main whose message marks them as AI-assisted.

stores.files: scores.sqlite (18 MB), descs.jsonl (the descriptions scored), and pilot result files.
stores.purpose: Haiku's estimate, per CL description, of whether it was AI-written.

tables.name: scores
tables.purpose: In scores.sqlite: one score per CL description.

columns.sha: Git commit hash of the Chromium change that was scored
columns.model: Model that scored the description, e.g. haiku
columns.prompt: Short hash identifying the scoring prompt version
columns.label: Marker class of the description: marked (AI-marked), unmarked, mid, or pre (before AI tools)
columns.chars: Length of the description in characters, footers stripped
columns.p: Model's probability that an AI agent wrote the description, 0-1

tables.withheld: The model's guess, per CL, of whether its description was AI-written; only aggregates are published.

tables.name: runs
tables.purpose: In scores.sqlite: each scoring run's cost.

columns.started_at: Time the scoring run started, Unix seconds
columns.prompt: Short hash identifying the prompt version used
columns.until_: Latest commit date scored; empty means no limit
columns.todo: Number of commits the run planned to score
columns.done: Number of commits scored so far
columns.usd: API cost of the run in US dollars
columns.finished_at: Time the run ended, Unix seconds; empty while running
columns.stopped: Reason the run stopped early, if it did; empty otherwise

stores.notes: Only scores.sqlite costs tokens to remake; the rest is rebuildable.

stores.purpose: Contributor clusters by working pattern, with a 2-D map of them.
Per-person career reports for a few exemplar contributors; private drafts behind docs/balance-person.md.
Every dataset the Review Balance page draws, as named aggregates with no per-person rows.
stores.notes: Written whole by balance-publish, whose STEPS list records the step behind each of its 92 datasets. Its window ends with the data (balance_publish.DATA_END: the first day of the month in which the newest fetched week ends).

stores.purpose: Balance measures per directory, for the page's directory table.
Author-level distributions for the page's author charts.

stores.name: Feedback Index data
stores.size: 126 MB (53 MB gzipped file by file, as git stores it)
stores.files: peers.json, u/<hash>.json (6,902 people, 122 other addresses) and <half-year>/<hash>.json (19 folders, 2017H2 .. 2026H2; before 2025H2 thread counts per directory, not each thread); <hash> is a salted SHA-256 of the e-mail.
stores.purpose: Per-person changes and addressed review comments, which the Feedback Index page fetches by a hash of the address typed, and peers.json with the feedback rates and index factors it compares them with.
stores.notes: Committed and published on GitHub Pages since 2026-11-12. Finished half-years' files don't change between runs unless their inputs do, so git stores them once; each run rewrites the current half-year, u/ and peers.json. Commit with `git add -A web/public/review-feedback/`.

stores.purpose: Private coaching reports that Opus writes from one person's review threads; never published.
stores.withheld: Private coaching reports about one person each; never published.

stores.size: 296 KB in 5 files, plus 18 KB in the 3 addressed_* files
stores.files: part1_report.json, part1_results.json, part2_results.json, reverts_results.json, substance_results.json; addressed_cl.json, addressed_blame.json, addressed_people.json (scripts/balance_addressed_value.py cl, blame and people --out).
stores.purpose: Result files of the review-ROI studies (does review feedback predict reverts and bugs) and of the addressed-index comparison, which balance-publish reads from these fixed names.
stores.notes: Copied here from the scripts' output (data/private/scratch/review_roi/); rerunning the studies is an analysis, not part of a publish.

stores.purpose: Scratch output of analysis scripts, one folder per topic; safe to delete.

stores.files: list/<month>/<n>.json.gz (2,906 search replies) and monorail/<month>/<n>.html.gz (21,267 stubs).
stores.purpose: Every tracker reply exactly as received.
stores.notes: Bug titles are untrusted: print counts and enums only.

stores.purpose: Which bugs are wanted and asked for, the request log, and the parsed metadata of visible bugs.

tables.name: wanted
tables.purpose: Bug IDs to ask for, with how many commits name each. Recomputed.

columns.id: Bug ID as written in a commit's Bug:/Fixed: footer or a Chrome Releases security post
columns.bug_commits: Number of main-branch commits naming this ID in a Bug: footer
columns.fixed_commits: Number of main-branch commits naming this ID in a Fixed: footer
columns.security: 1 if the ID appears in Chrome Releases security fixes, else 0
columns.first_commit: Committer date of the earliest commit that names this ID, ISO 8601
columns.last_commit: Committer date of the latest commit that names this ID, ISO 8601

tables.name: asked
tables.purpose: Per ID: whether it was visible and when it was asked. Fetch history.

columns.visible: 1 if the tracker returned the bug, 0 if it was restricted or absent
columns.first_asked: Time of the first request that asked for this ID, UTC ISO 8601
columns.last_asked: Time of the most recent request that asked for this ID, UTC ISO 8601
columns.times: How many requests have asked for this ID
columns.request_seq: Sequence number of the last request that asked for this ID

tables.name: monorail_map
tables.purpose: Old Monorail ID to new tracker ID. Fetch history.

columns.old_id: Old Monorail-era bug ID that we looked up
columns.new_id: Issue-tracker ID the old ID redirects to; empty if the stub names no issue
columns.http_status: HTTP status code of the lookup reply
columns.fetched_at: Time of the lookup, UTC ISO 8601
columns.request_seq: Sequence number of the request that did the lookup

tables.name: requests
tables.purpose: One row per HTTP request and its outcome. Fetch history.

columns.seq: Request sequence number, counting up from 1
columns.kind: Request type: list (batch of issue IDs) or monorail (old-ID lookup)
columns.started_at: Time the request started, UTC ISO 8601
columns.http_status: HTTP status code of the reply; -1 means a network error
columns.request_body: What we sent: the bug IDs asked for
columns.body_bytes: Size of the reply body in bytes after decompression
columns.file: Path of the saved gzip copy of the reply, under bugs/raw/
columns.n_asked: Number of bug IDs the request asked for
columns.n_returned: Number of bugs the reply contained
columns.outcome: Result class: ok, http (error status), shape (unexpected reply), blocked, or net (network error)

tables.name: bugs
tables.purpose: Parsed metadata of each visible bug. Rebuildable from raw/ with `parse`.

columns.tracker: Numeric ID of the tracker the issue lives in (157 is Chromium); sometimes empty
columns.component_id: Numeric ID of the bug's component
columns.component_path: Component name path, e.g. a slash-separated hierarchy
columns.type: Numeric bug type (1 Bug, 2 Feature request, 6 Vulnerability, ...)
columns.type_name: Name of the bug type; empty for unknown codes
columns.status: Numeric status (1 New ... 4 Fixed, 5 Verified, 10 Duplicate)
columns.status_name: Name of the status, e.g. New, Assigned, Fixed
columns.title: Bug title (untrusted text from the tracker)
columns.created: Time the bug was filed, UTC ISO 8601
columns.modified: Time of the last change to the bug, UTC ISO 8601
columns.resolved: Time the bug was closed, UTC ISO 8601; empty if open
columns.verified: Time the fix was verified, UTC ISO 8601; only on Verified bugs
columns.cve: CVE identifier assigned to the bug, if any
columns.introduced_in: Version or milestone where the bug was introduced (custom field)
columns.milestone: Chrome milestone the bug targets or was fixed in (custom field)
columns.security_release: Security release the fix shipped in (custom field)
columns.os: Operating systems the bug affects (custom field)
columns.labels: Chromium labels on the bug, comma-separated (untrusted text)
columns.found_in: Chrome milestones the bug was found in, as a JSON list
columns.hotlists: IDs of hotlists containing the bug, as a JSON list
columns.fixed_by: Code changes that fixed the bug, as a JSON list of host/project/change
columns.fixed_by_field: Display text of the Fixed By Code Changes custom field
columns.regression: 1 if labelled regression or Introduced In is set, else 0 (rough heuristic)
columns.custom: All custom fields as a JSON map of name to value (untrusted text)
columns.raw_file: Saved raw reply file this record was parsed from
columns.fetched_at: Time the record was fetched, UTC ISO 8601

stores.notes: Mixes fetch history that can't be rebuilt with two tables that can.

stores.name: Chrome releases
stores.files: raw/page-NNNN.json (26 feed pages), security_fixes.json, fixing_commits.json, summary.json.
stores.purpose: The Chrome Releases feed, the security fixes parsed from it, and the commits on main that fixed them.
stores.notes: Only raw/ is fetched; the three JSON files are rebuilt from it.

stores.purpose: This inventory, kept by hand whenever a source, store, step or page changes.
stores.notes: `python3 scripts/dataflow.py check` verifies it against the repository.

steps.command: python3 -m cosh backfill --weeks 1 --newest <week> --go; python3 -m cosh extract-open
steps.purpose: Fetches closed CLs week by week (listings over REST, review history as NoteDb refs) and snapshots the open ones.
steps.incremental: Skips listing windows and refs already fetched; a finished week is skipped. Each extract-open run lists open CLs updated since the last complete snapshot.
steps.duration: about 22 min per week (18.8 h for 52 weeks)
steps.approval: Only weeks in config/approved.json (2017-W27 .. 2026-W44); the command refuses others. A newer week needs the user's approval, then an edit to that file.
steps.notes: backfill --weeks N runs many weeks, newest first; long runs go in a systemd user service (CLAUDE.md). backfill also derives each week it finishes (cosh.derive for that week), so reviews.sqlite stays current between full derives. Never run alongside another extractor.

steps.purpose: Copies Chromium's affiliations.json5 and org-list.txt into config/ when they have changed.
steps.incremental: Rewrites only on a change.
steps.duration: seconds
steps.notes: The one step that fetches them: the commands that attribute orgs (summarize, comments-collect, review-feedback, balance-publish) read the local copy, so `cosh update` runs this first.

steps.purpose: Reduces every CL's listing and NoteDb comments to facts.
steps.incremental: Not incremental: a full run re-reads every CL. `--week W` does one week.
steps.duration: under 52 min for 1.6M CLs; 11.5 min for 775k
steps.cost_source: File times of the 2026-11-12 run (upper bound); docs/plan.md, 2026-11-05
steps.notes: Opens gerrit.sqlite read-only, so it is safe beside an extractor. Main's commits are in commits.sqlite (step commits), not here.

steps.purpose: Has sandboxed Haiku label the threads the regex doesn't settle as addressed or not.
steps.incremental: Only threads with no label for the current classifier and input hash; saved per batch, so it resumes.
steps.duration: about 11 min per week; 41 min per year at 8 calls at once
steps.token_cost: about 0.95M Haiku tokens per week ($0.22); 25.6M per year ($6); about 290 per thread (2017 .. 2021: 408k threads, 119M tokens, 2.5 h, $26)
steps.approval: Costs Max usage: check --dry-run first (it underestimates by about a third). No labels for 2017 .. 2021.
steps.notes: A week shows the addressed metric only once it is 99% labelled, so the site's default metric needs this for each new week.

steps.purpose: Aggregates the facts and labels into the Value Exchange summaries for every fetched week.
steps.incremental: Rewrites every file for all weeks.
steps.notes: It reads the raw stores for the example threads' text.

steps.purpose: Lossless housekeeping of the NoteDb repo: packs refs and indexes its packs, so reads stay fast.
steps.incremental: Deletes nothing.
steps.duration: 41 min for the chunked repack of 3,823 packs into 14
steps.approval: Never prune. The chunked repack keeps the old packs until a person has checked the new ones.
steps.notes: For thousands of packs use scripts/notedb_chunked_repack.sh (700 MB groups); a whole-repo repack runs out of memory.

steps.purpose: Audits the addressed classifier against Opus, and the earlier research that chose the classifier and the Commits metric.
steps.duration: 32 Opus calls for 800 threads
steps.notes: scripts/comment_classifier.py still carries an older copy of the prompt than cosh/classify.py.

steps.purpose: Fetches chromium/src main into the shared clone, so new weeks' commits reach commits.sqlite.
steps.incremental: Fetches only what main gained since the last fetch.
steps.approval: main only (approved 2026-11-06); other branches or repos need approval.
steps.notes: The clone's README says cosh does these fetches. Run it before `cosh commits` when a new week is processed.

steps.purpose: Appends main's new commits, with their files, line counts, LSC tags, OWNERS additions and repetition ratios, to the commits store.
steps.incremental: Appends the commits landed since its last run; seconds when nothing is new.
steps.duration: about 1 h 50 min from empty (1.5 h of git log, then 20 min of OWNERS diffs and repetition ratios with 4 processes); seconds when nothing is new
steps.notes: Run it after the shared clone gains commits; nothing in cosh updates the clone. It replaces `cosh.balance git`, derive's commits tables and the hand-made balance inputs.

steps.purpose: Fetches every patch set of reviewed CLs, newest first, into the patch-set repo.
steps.incremental: Resumable. A CL is fetched again when Gerrit has more patch sets than were fetched (cosh-fetched.txt records the count).
steps.duration: 72 s per 1,000 CLs
steps.approval: Only reviewed CLs in config/approved.json's range (closed 2023-06-26 .. 2026-11-02); the command refuses an earlier --since. Up to 7 fetches at once (approved 2026-11-07).
steps.notes: Repack afterwards in groups with the two scripts; never prune.

steps.purpose: Fetches the Radar quarters that are missing or incomplete and rewrites the browser-share CSV.
steps.incremental: Complete quarters are skipped; `--offline` rebuilds the CSV from the cache alone.
steps.duration: about 3 requests, a few seconds
steps.approval: Approved. Never print or commit the token.

steps.command: python3 -m cosh.sentiment collect --missing (or --week <weeks>; --sample 0.05 --name sample-5pct for the trend's sample)
steps.purpose: Renders each week's review comments with their thread context and who wrote them, ready for scoring.
steps.incremental: Rewrites the week files it is given.
steps.duration: about 25 s per week; 2 min for the 5% sample
steps.notes: --missing collects every fetched week since the oldest week file that has no file yet.

steps.purpose: Has Haiku score each rendered comment's tone and AI friction, in the sandbox.
steps.incremental: Skips comments already scored under the same prompt; saved per batch.
steps.duration: 3 to 4 min per week; 37 min for the 5% sample
steps.token_cost: about $1.25 of Haiku per week; 21.9M tokens ($5.48) for the 5% sample
steps.approval: Costs Max usage: size runs with --name or --week.

steps.purpose: Writes every Review Tone file from the newest year of fully scored weeks.
steps.incremental: Rewrites every file. Screening verdicts are cached in sentiment.sqlite, so only new comments cost model calls.
steps.token_cost: small, not measured; nothing once the cache has the comments
steps.approval: Publishes names for praise only; never negative figures per person or org (docs/sentiment.md).
steps.notes: The window follows the data: the newest run of up to 52 consecutive fully scored weeks (sentiment.scored_weeks). It also writes the screening cache (sentiment.sqlite's screens), which is not drawn as an output so the scores keep one writer.

steps.purpose: Scores a prompt version against the 261 gold comments, to tune the prompt.
Reads each CL's uploads, attention-set changes and Code-Review votes from NoteDb.
steps.incremental: Reads CLs not yet read and CLs whose meta ref's tip moved since (replacing their rows); CLs without a ref are looked for again next time.
steps.duration: 35.5 min (330 CLs/s, sharing the box with another git walk) for 716k CLs from empty

steps.purpose: Diffs each patch set against the next to measure rework during review.
steps.incremental: Only CLs without a result; CLs whose patch sets aren't fetched get none.
steps.duration: about 25 min as three shards

steps.purpose: Joins the stages into one row per CL.
steps.incremental: Rebuilds the whole table.
steps.duration: about 2 min for 1.14M CLs

steps.purpose: Lists the commits whose messages mark them as AI-assisted.
steps.duration: about 1 min

steps.command: python3 scripts/balance_ai_predict.py build && nice -n 5 python3 scripts/balance_ai_predict.py score --since 2025-07-01
steps.purpose: Has sandboxed Haiku estimate, for each CL description, whether it was AI-written.
steps.incremental: `score` resumes: descriptions already scored are skipped.
steps.duration: 116 min for 171,804 CLs at 8 calls at once

steps.purpose: Groups contributors' half-years into activity patterns and trajectories (k-means over private per-person panels), and maps the patterns.
steps.incremental: Recomputes everything.
steps.duration: about 10 min
steps.notes: An analysis kept as an input of balance-publish (its per-person people.json stays private); rerun it before a publish when the clusters should follow new data.

steps.purpose: Writes the Review Balance page's three files whole, from empty, by running each dataset's compute function in the order its STEPS list records.
steps.incremental: Recomputes everything; --steps a,b reruns only those steps and reuses the others' results in data/private/scratch/balance-publish/steps/.
steps.duration: about 10 min (revert_experience 3 of them, measured 2026-11-13 at nice 5), about 5 GB of memory at most (one step at a time)
steps.notes: Its window ends at balance_publish.DATA_END (2026-11-01; D3 decides whether it follows new weeks). --check rebuilds into the scratch directory and compares with the committed files, dataset by dataset. Reads balance_clusters/, chrome_releases/summary.json and review_roi/ as finished analyses; everything else is computed on each run.

steps.command: python3 scripts/balance_analysis.py trends|growth|pipeline; scripts/balance_ai.py paired|did|footers; scripts/balance_person.py; scripts/balance_exemplars.py; scripts/balance_explore.py
steps.purpose: Exploratory analyses behind the balance docs: trends, AI effects, per-person career reports.
steps.duration: 3 to 5 min and several GB of memory each
steps.token_cost: small Haiku pilots, about $0.06 per 1,000 CLs
steps.notes: Results go into docs/balance*.md by hand. Network use is the model pilots only.

steps.purpose: Writes each person's changes and addressed review comments, as files named by a hash of their address, and the feedback rates and index factors the page compares them with.
steps.incremental: Deletes and rewrites every file.
steps.duration: about 2 min (119 s on 2026-11-14), 3 GB of memory
steps.approval: Tone is praise only (docs/plan.md, ground rule 5).
steps.notes: Computes its per-CL facts (owner, status, Gerrit size, landed commit, lines per directory) from reviews.sqlite and commits.sqlite (cosh.cl_facts). Earlier commits count from 2008. Its tone year is Review Tone's (sentiment.scored_weeks). It refreshes the affiliations file first (its only network use). `npm run serve` picks the new files up a few seconds after the run ends.

steps.purpose: Has sandboxed Opus write a private coaching report from one person's recent review threads.
steps.incremental: `--reuse` rebuilds the report from the saved reply without a new call.
steps.duration: about 1 min per report
steps.approval: Costs Max usage; reports are never published.

steps.command: python3 scripts/review_roi_table.py ...; review_roi_depth.py; review_roi_later_changes.py; review_roi_blame.py; review_roi_reverts.py; review_roi_substance.py
steps.purpose: The review-ROI studies: whether review feedback predicts later reverts, bug-fixing commits and security bugs; and the addressed index against the feedback index.
steps.duration: about 1 h; the full blame runs were estimated at 10 to 16 CPU hours
steps.token_cost: Haiku pilots only: 274 tokens per thread, 200 threads
steps.notes: The scripts write to data/private/scratch/review_roi/ by default; the results balance-publish reads are copied into data/private/review_roi/ by hand (the addressed ones as addressed_cl.json, addressed_blame.json, addressed_people.json). This is the only path by which bug-tracker data reaches a page.

steps.command: python3 scripts/review_impact.py --weeks 2026-W36:2026-W44 --out threads.jsonl; python3 scripts/review_impact_stats.py threads.jsonl
steps.purpose: Early study of which review threads change the CL, behind docs/review-impact.md.
steps.duration: about 25 s

steps.purpose: Fetches the Chrome Releases feed, parses its security fixes and joins them to their fixing commits on main.
steps.incremental: Fetches only pages it lacks, so the newest page goes stale without --refresh; parse and join recompute.
steps.duration: about 1 min of fetching (26 requests)

steps.purpose: Lists the bug IDs to ask for, from commit footers on main and the security fixes.
steps.incremental: Recomputes the wanted table.
steps.duration: about 10 s

steps.command: nice -n 5 python3 -m cosh.bugs fetch --go && nice -n 5 python3 -m cosh.bugs monorail --go && nice -n 5 python3 -m cosh.bugs fetch --go
steps.purpose: Asks the tracker for every wanted bug not asked yet, maps old Monorail IDs, then asks for those too.
steps.incremental: Only IDs never asked; `fetch --retry-missing` re-asks invisible ones after 30 days. `parse` rebuilds the bugs table from raw/ offline.
steps.duration: about 1.5 h in all: 2,906 searches and 21,267 stub lookups
steps.approval: Approved 2026-11-08 for bugs in footers since 2023-07-01 and security fixes. Other trackers or b: bugs need approval.
